title: Ontologies in Design: How Imagining a Tree Reveals Possibilites and Assumptions in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative prompting of four LLM chatbots (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Copilot, Bard) using 14 targeted questions to uncover their default philosophical assumptions, alongside a critical analysis (hermeneutic reverse engineering) of an LLM-based agent architecture ('Generative Agents') to reveal embedded assumptions about cognition, memory, and humanness.

Evaluating LLM chatbot responses to assess whether they default to Western philosophical traditions and analyzing how they generalize, stereotype, or group non-Western, Indigenous, and African ontologies when explicitly prompted to consider alternative worldviews.

Analyzing the design of the 'Generative Agents' cognitive architecture to highlight how its rigid structures for memory, reflection, and planning oversimplify human cognition, pathologize neurodivergence, and assume a universal, post-Enlightenment rationalist model of intelligence.
